question: How much do all the bacteria living in an adult's body weigh together?
answer: About 200 grams. A 2016 recount put the bacteria in a 70 kg man at about 38 trillion, nearly all in the colon, close to his 30 trillion human cells. Being tiny, they weigh about 0.2 kg, near 0.3% of the body. One bowel movement empties a quarter to a third of them.
move: Before repeating a striking figure, ask when someone last measured it.
trap: The figure of one to two kilograms, repeated for decades.
